fixes.old: While ACE ingestion is still on Control-M, rwb-source-data polls the ACE batch record as the fallback.
fixes.new: While ACE ingestion is still on Control-M, rwb-source-data polls the ACE batch record as the fallback. Airflow is recorded at Recovery's edges only, and the Control-M poll stays as the fallback until a new ADR replaces the BRD's ADF and Control-M wording (GAP-0009).

fixes.old: Version 1.30 or later, because Nexus and Worker Versioning are needed, on the pinned release SCB IT approves at build.
fixes.new: Version 1.30 or later, because Nexus and Worker Versioning are needed, on the pinned release SCB IT approves at build. One release of 1.30 or later is pinned in Wave 0 and recorded in this ADR and in the Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1; the exact release number is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0091).

fixes.old: - The call type is chosen by four questions in order: a person waiting is REST; a fact others may react to is an event; a step another service must perform with a result is a Temporal activity or child workflow; bulk data or a party outside the bank is a file through rwb-integration. ACE data is asked of rwb-source-data, in REST for a screen and as an activity in a workflow.
fixes.new: - The Architecture v5 rule that route services reach shared capabilities through Temporal, never REST, covers the five shared capabilities: decision, document, payment, partner and comms. The route services' reference reads from rwb-source-data stay REST, one hop and cached (GAP-0104).

fixes.old: The amendment to T1 and T2 of D-RCV-36 is recorded here by reference to the mapping in Template and Rules §R8.4; the Change Register text itself is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0090; ASM-0152).
fixes.new:
The amendment to T1 and T2 of D-RCV-36 follows the mapping in Template and Rules §R8.4. The text being amended, from the Temporal and Drools Change Register v1 (GAP-0090), is:

- T1: "Temporal, hybrid. Case data stays the system of record in the ACE DB recovery schema. Temporal runs the case lifecycle from Epic 3: one workflow per case, plus durable timers, retries and automated multi-step chains. Self-hosted on the shared ACE AKS clusters in the ACE namespace."
- T2: "Quartz and Spring Batch stay for every Epic 1 and Epic 2 scheduled job (JOB-03 allocation, JOB-04 reconciliation, JOB-05 timer check, JOB-06 rebalance, JOB-07, JOB-08 and the rest). JOB-05 runs behind a new TimerScheduler port so that Epic 3 can swap in Temporal durable timers without changing callers. Temporal Schedules are not used in Epics 1 and 2."

Wave 0 pin recorded in ADR-016; exact release number not invented. The Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1 needs the same entry.
Reading of the rule added to the ADR-020 Decision.
